title: Implement PEP 639 license expression canonicalization in packaging at pinned 24.1
goal: Clone https://github.com/pypa/packaging into work/gc-345/repo (relative to the benchmark repo root) and check out pinned commit 85442b8032cb7bae72866dfd7782234a98dd2fb7 (release tag 24.1); the grader verifies that HEAD equals this exact commit, so keep all repairs as uncommitted working-tree edits to non-test source files. At this commit there is no packaging.licenses module. The sealed tests require canonicalize_license_expression() to validate and case-normalize SPDX license expressions: bare ids, OR/AND composition, parenthesized nesting, the '+' suffix, WITH exception clauses, and LicenseRef passthrough, raising InvalidLicenseExpression on malformed or unknown input. This requires assembling SPDX license and exception id tables plus an expression parser, not string tricks. Decompose the work into a written plan, run the grader command first to record the initial RED state and the identities of the failing sealed tests, implement incrementally, and re-run the exact grader command after each increment until all 7 sealed tests pass. Do not edit or shadow anything under assets/gc-345/: the grader re-copies the sealed tests from assets over the workspace and disables pytest plugin autoloading and conftest collection, so test tampering cannot turn the run GREEN.

spec.command: git config --global --add safe.directory '*' && test "$(git -C work/gc-345/repo rev-parse HEAD)" = "85442b8032cb7bae72866dfd7782234a98dd2fb7" && pip -q install pytest==8.2.2 && pip -q install --no-deps ./work/gc-345/repo && rm -rf work/gc-345/sealed_run && mkdir -p work/gc-345/sealed_run && cp assets/gc-345/tests/*.py work/gc-345/sealed_run/ && cd work/gc-345/sealed_run && PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 python -m pytest -q --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider .

process_expectations: A written repair plan exists at work/gc-345/notes/plan.md before the first source edit, naming the target module(s) and the sealed tests each step is meant to turn green.
The grader command was executed once before any source change and its RED output (failing sealed test identities, not just counts) is preserved verbatim in the run log.
A running log at work/gc-345/notes/attempts.md maps each code iteration to the specific sealed test identities it targeted and what the re-verification run returned.
After any RED re-verification the next diff is traceable to a named failing test, not a blind full rewrite; abandoned approaches are recorded rather than deleted.
An honest cost/time ledger covering all attempts, including failed ones, is kept alongside the notes.
